sources.note: Scores unlabeled reasoning trajectories by how their mean-pooled hidden states connect to correct and incorrect reference point clouds built from a small labeled set, and uses that score to pick the concrete chosen and rejected responses inside answer clusters that self-consistency has already separated.
sources.title: Cloud-ScPO: Hidden-State Geometry for Semi-Supervised Preference Optimization in LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Feeds a reasoning model's own self-certainty into preference optimization so it compresses confident answers and keeps deliberating on uncertain ones.
sources.title: CAT: Confidence-Adaptive Thinking for Efficient Reasoning of Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Reframes unlearning in reasoning models as an intervention on the CoT itself, having the model generate logically valid counterfactual traces and iteratively preference-tuning toward them.
sources.title: CiPO: Counterfactual Unlearning for Large Reasoning Models through Iterative Preference Optimization

sources.note: Prunes chain-of-thought segments the model's own likelihood landscape marks as extraneous, then trains on the resulting pruning preference pairs.
sources.title: Your Reasoning Model Knows What Counts: Self-Guided Chain-of-Thought Pruning for Efficient Reasoning

sources.note: Builds a large standardized meta-benchmark and finds that LLM-judge preference scores do not correlate with concrete measures of safety, world knowledge or instruction following, because judges systematically prioritize style over factuality and safety.
sources.title: Style Outweighs Substance: Failure Modes of LLM Judges in Alignment Benchmarking

result.definition: Training on comparisons between outputs rather than on scalar rewards or gold targets, and across 5 sources a family whose design question is what the pair is drawn from. The corpus's instances differ exactly there: pairs selected inside answer clusters that consensus has already separated, using hidden-state geometry to pick which concrete responses to compare; pairs of correct trajectories ranked by a redundancy score; pairs formed between a repair and the continuation that would have followed had an error stood; and counterfactual pairs for unlearning. Two findings. The pairing is the constraint -- two responses may not form a usable pair, which makes the method data-hungry where an unpaired objective keeps improving at one response per instruction. And a preference term added to group-relative training can hurt: a matched baseline with an unweighted term added falls below the base model on four of six benchmarks.
